title: TESS eclipse times of 557 southern ACVS binaries (P = 5-22 d) show common-mode third-body timing variations in 14; Gaia DR3 gives accelerations for 2 of these 14 and for 1 of 393 quiet binaries
abstract: Earlier campaign work found fading eclipses in HD 303514 with a depth screen of ACVS binaries, and later work found that a third star on a 1.6-year orbit moves its eclipse times by about 100 minutes. The depth screen did not measure eclipse times. We measured 14,726 eclipse times in TESS QLP light curves (2018-2026) of 557 detached ACVS binaries with periods of 5-22 days. Separate linear ephemerides for primary and secondary eclipses remove linear apsidal motion; we then searched for timing changes common to both eclipse types. Both positive controls were found (HD 303514 common-mode, HD 93683 apsidal-like). 29 of 515 measured binaries pass common-mode rules and 14 pass stricter rules (range at least 15 minutes, primary-only range at least 10 minutes; ranges 16-120 minutes). Sector timing offsets in 441 quiet binaries are at most 2.6 minutes. Gaia DR3 gives astrometric acceleration solutions for 2 of the 14 robust systems (ASAS J090232-5653.4 and HD 104856) but for only 1 of 393 quiet binaries (one-sided Fisher p = 0.003); for HD 104856 the timing amplitude and the Gaia acceleration agree in size. Robust detection fractions are 2-4 percent per period bin. Only HD 303514 needs a light-travel-time velocity change above 20 km/s, consistent with its published dynamical origin. An independent three-body search for HD 303514 recovers the published 600-day family and predicts the 2026 eclipse times to 5 minutes from 2019-2025 data. Limitations: QLP photometry only, rules set after a first visual inspection, no orbit fits for the new systems, and a limited literature check.
